title: First round
text: Let $$u=x^3$$ and $$dv=sin\left(x\right) dx$$. This gives $$-x^3 cos\left(x\right)$$ plus the integral of $$3x^2 cos\left(x\right)$$.

title: Keep going
text: Use integration by parts two more times. The integral of $$3x^2 cos\left(x\right)$$ is $$3x^2 sin\left(x\right)+6x cos\left(x\right)-6sin\left(x\right)$$.
